ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3–462.5 and s. 462.31 (money laundering offences); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-146, as amended, including beneficial-ownership amendments SOR/2022-81 effective 15 December 2022 (identification of individuals owning or controlling 25% or more of an entity); Limited Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 347 (especially ss. 38, 42 and 43 concerning records, registered office, and partner registers); Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 and its regulations (supplementary transparency and records requirements for BC-registered entities); Land Owner Transparency Act, S.B.C. 2019, c. 23 (applicable if the LP ever acquires an interest in land in BC); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, S.C. 1995, c. 19; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2011, c. 30, s. 2; FINTRAC Guidance on Beneficial Ownership Reporting (FINTRAC, current PCMLTFA interpretive guidance).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Passport (bio-data page) of each individual general partner and each limited-partner UBO, for FINTRAC record keeping and BC registry partner-signature verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, commissioner for taking affidavits, or lawyer admitted in the partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin (Hague Apostille Convention in force for Canada since 11 January 2024) OR consular legalization through the receiving state's consulate for states not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certified Registry Extract for any corporate general partner or corporate UBO-entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or ministry in the entity's governing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent foreign authority OR consular legalization; for Canadian-issued extracts, apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Residential Address (utility bill or regulated bank statement dated within 60 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or bank regulated in the partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, where required by the BC registry or the LP's payment processor/institution, Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Consent to Act as General Partner and Signing Authority Certificate (executed under British Columbia law)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Lawyer or notary public admitted in British Columbia
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Prepared and notarized in BC; Global Affairs Canada apostille required only if the document is later filed in a foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all general partners, named limited partners, and 25%+ UBOs against: (i) OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and OFAC Consolidated Sanctions Lists; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and its associated resolutions; (iii) Canadian sanctions and entity determinations under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the United Nations Act; (iv) domestic PEP / foreign PEP / Heads of International Organizations categorization under s. 9.3 of SOR/2002-146, including enhanced continuous monitoring where a PEP owns 25% or more of the LP; (v) Canadian bankruptcy, insolvency, criminal-record, and enforcement-order checks through FINTRAC-compliant due diligence tools. The business is classified as Low_Risk_Standard (handmade tabletop gaming accessories sold through Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal). The LP must still adopt a written AML/CFT compliance program within 30 days of first transaction, appoint a compliance officer, and maintain customer/beneficial-ownership records for five years under PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services — OneStop Business Registry (bcregistry.gov.bc.ca; www.bcregistry.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC limited partnership name must consist of English or French words or a combination of both, expressed in Latin alphabet characters; non-Latin script names are accepted only with a mandatory transliteration consistent with the pre-clearance NUANS name search report. The name must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing BC-registered names, trademarks, or federal names. The legal ending must be 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'LP', 'Société en commandite', 'S.E.C.', or 'SEC'. Punctuation, numerals, and abbreviations are governed by Part 3 of the BC Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 222/2004. Generic commodity descriptors such as 'epoxy', 'dice', or 'maker' do not, by themselves, create distinctiveness.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Term or expression suggesting a connection with a public body, professional regulator, or royal/state authority absent prior ministerial or professional-body consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the filer receives a formal refusal notice through the BC Registries OnLine portal. The filer may: (1) cure the defects and file a new name-request with a fresh NUANS search; (2) within 30 days of the refusal, file a written reconsideration request with the BC Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry, PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC) identifying the name reservation number, the exact name applied for, and annexing legal authorities, trademark evidence, and letters of consent; or (3) for decisions that are ultra vires or unreasonable, commence judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 24, within 60 days of the decision. The registrar's administrative reconsideration decision is final unless judicial review is commenced.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for a BC limited partnership provided the nominated office is a physical street address in British Columbia (not a P.O. Box), open to the public during normal business hours (typically 09:00–16:30), and staffed by an agent authorized to accept service of process and government mail. For a low-risk homemade epoxy-dice maker selling via Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal, a virtual-office lease is commercially reasonable and does not trigger automatic registry inspection. The LP must maintain its general-ledger, partnership, and beneficial-ownership records at the registered office or at a stated alternative records place in BC, and must produce those records to the Registrar, FINTRAC, CRA, or police on lawful demand. No statutory minimum office square footage or employee requirement applies; substance requirements are minimal for a pass-through LP, but the maker must respect home-expense deduction rules and Canada Revenue Agency's general anti-avoidance framework if claiming business use of home.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — assessed annualized on-site inspection probability of 3–5% during the first 12 months. BC Registry does not conduct unannounced physical inspections of limited partnerships. Canada Revenue Agency desktop audit risk for a low-revenue single-maker commodity operation is approximately 2–4%. WorkSafeBC inspection likelihood rises to approximately 8–10% if an injury claim is filed by a courier or contractor or if epoxy-resin chemical handling is suspected under the Workers Compensation Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 492. Canada Border Services Agency may conduct physical goods examination at the border if resin is imported in commercial quantities, but this is not a business-premises inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 227, ss. 3-6 (declaration, registration, name, records office), read with the Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348; Business Names Act, RSBC 1996, c. 57 for name-clearance matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of British Columbia (Corporate Online / CS Online self-service portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) - the statutory application for registration of the limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a BC limited partnership; each limited partner's contribution (cash, property, or services binding as an obligation) is fixed solely by the Limited Partnership Agreement, and no escrow or trust account is mandated by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF GOLDEN GAIT LP - [DATE]. WHEREAS the GP is authorized to form a limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 227; RESOLVED: 1. The GP shall execute and file the Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) with the BC Registrar of Companies. 2. Limited partners' capital contributions, per Schedule A of the Limited Partnership Agreement, are hereby accepted; no escrow is required. 3. The registered records office is fixed at Suite 210, 888 Homer Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 0C3. 4. [Officer 1] is appointed managing general partner, [Officer 2] secretary-treasurer, and [Officer 3] compliance officer, each authorized to open bank accounts and execute filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services - Corporate Online Name Reservation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one primary and one alternate proposed LP name via Corporate Online; the name must include 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered BC name; pay the non-refundable reservation fee (approx. CAD 30); the reservation is valid for 56 days and may be used for the Form LP1 filing.
required_dossiers: Consent to Use of Name (if requested by Registrar)
Written authorization from the general partner to make the reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, the Registrar issues a refusal notice; counsel may re-file an amended name request within the same 56-day window or submit written submissions under the Business Names Act; a revised name normally clears within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Solicitor of record and all partners (private execution; no registry filing at this substep)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement before a notary public in BC, specifying the general partner's exclusive management authority, each limited partner's capital contribution and profit share, restrictions on limited-partner participation in control, withdrawal provisions, and the registered records office address; the executed Contribution Schedule must be prepared as the underlying record for the Form LP1 declaration.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (wet-ink or electronic signatures)
Consent of the General Partner to Act (Form LP1 attachment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a limited partner defaults on an agreed contribution, the general partner issues a formal default notice and amends the Limited Partnership Agreement by supplementary deed; the revised contribution schedule is subsequently filed as an amendment under s. 14 of the Limited Partnership Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Form LP1 and Issuance of Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies - Corporate Online (CS Online) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP1 electronically, providing the reserved LP name, BC registered records office street address, full names and addresses of the general and all limited partners, aggregate capital contribution, and the term (if not perpetual); pay the CAD 40 registration fee; the Registrar issues an electronic Certificate of Limited Partnership Registration with a unique LP registration number upon approval.
required_dossiers: Consent to Registered Records Office Address (landlord consent form)
Certified copy of the notarized general-partner resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is placed in correction status due to a deficiency (e.g., name mismatch, incomplete partner address), the filer corrects the flagged field and re-submits within 10 business days to avoid a fresh fee; escalated queries are resolved by the Registrar's registry support desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number, GST/HST and BC PST Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); BC Ministry of Finance - Provincial Tax Programs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the LP's CRA Business Number (BN) using the Certificate of Limited Partnership Registration; register for GST/HST once quarterly gross revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 and for BC PST where retail sales of RPG dice occur; file annually the T50 Partnership Information Return; the LP is pass-through for tax, and non-resident limited partners hold no statutory public-officeholder residency condition.
required_dossiers: Banking KYC pack for Stripe and PayPal settlement accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the BN application due to entity-name mismatch, reconcile the legal name with the Certificate and re-submit through Business Registration Online; for PST, a voluntary registration may be backdated up to six months upon written request to the BC Ministry of Finance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Records Office Maintenance, Annual Reports and Governance Fixity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies - Annual Report Division; the LP's registered records keeper
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Post-registration, the general partner must maintain at the declared BC records office the Limited Partnership Agreement, register of limited partners, contribution records, and partnership minutes; file the first annual report within 60 days after the registration anniversary (approx. CAD 10 fee); ensure all contracts, bank accounts, and licence documents state the exact registered LP name.
required_dossiers: Registered records office address consent (retained on file)
Copy of the Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual report is late, the Registrar may strike the LP; the cure is a late annual report plus a reinstatement application under the Partnership Act within the grace period; any records-office relocation requires a Form LP2 change filing with the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (BC) - Environmental Management Branch; municipal planning and development department (e.g., City of Vancouver Development & Building Services) for local business and occupancy permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no provincial manufacturing or industrial operating permit is separately mandated for hand-craft scale epoxy dice casting (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930); a municipal business licence and, for commercial premises, a building occupancy permit are required for the casting studio.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy - Environmental Management Branch (with WorkSafeBC for occupational co-oversight)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration-Only - the cottage-scale epoxy casting operation sits below the threshold of an Environmental Assessment Certificate under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2018, c. 51; at most a municipal sewer-registration under the Municipal Wastewater Regulation (BC Reg. 87/2012) is triggered if process washwater is discharged to the sanitary sewer.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal Wastewater Regulation (BC Reg. 87/2012) sewer-use limits: pH 6.0-9.5; BOD5 <= 300 mg/L; TSS <= 350 mg/L; no free or emulsified oil above 20 mg/L; VOC/odour from uncured epoxy resin and hardener must not create a nuisance under ss. 59-61 of the Environmental Management Act; fully cured resin waste may be disposed as municipal waste per BC Landfill Criteria (BC Reg. 185/2016), while uncured resin and hardener spill residues are recorded as small-quantity hazardous residues with SDS documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC occupational clearance under the Workers Compensation Act and OHS Regulation (BC Reg. 296/97): SDS binder, mechanical ventilation for resin vapours, and nitrile glove/eye-protection PPE; BC Fire Code (BC Reg. 213/2007) certification for storage of flammable accelerants and curing-oven heat sources; structural load inspection where industrial kilns or ovens are installed; municipal building occupancy permit and business licence issued by the local government.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal income tax and GST/HST; portal: CRA My Business Account / Business Registration Online. BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch — BC PST administration (no single-window federal/provincial fiscal portal exists).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Register the BC limited partnership with BC Registries under the British Columbia Limited Partnership Act to obtain the BC LP registration number. 2. Apply to CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with GST/HST (RT) and/or income tax program accounts using Form RC1 or through an authorized representative in CRA's Represent a Client system. 3. Add a BC PST account through the BC provincial tax portal once taxable retail activities in BC commence. 4. For export goods, obtain/register a CBSA exporter identifier and file export declarations through the Export Reporting System. The BN serves as the Canadian TIN; CRA will issue separate program accounts for GST/HST, payroll, and income tax; a GST/HST registrant must quote the BN-RT on commercial invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election and no discretionary entity classification regime. A BC LP is per se transparent for Canadian income tax: profits and losses flow to partners and are taxed in the partners' hands; no entity-level federal income tax is imposed on the LP. For GST/HST, the partnership itself is a 'person' and must hold its own registration; no election can change that liability. Certain routine elections (partnership taxation-year alignment and GST/HST related-party filing elections) are available, but no hybrid mismatch election can reclassify the LP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST/HST (5% GST in BC; no HST) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (7% PST); BC uses a split consumption-tax system with separate GST and PST returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (GST/HST small-supplier threshold over any four consecutive calendar quarters of worldwide taxable supplies; BC PST registration has no comparable general dollar threshold for BC vendors making taxable retail sales).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable. Canada and BC do not mandate real-time electronic invoice clearance, fiscal stamping, or API-based government server reporting. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically by registrants with taxable annual revenues exceeding C$1,500,000; all accounting and export evidence must be kept in English or French for six years and be available to CRA/CBSA on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods (RPG dice) are zero-rated under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act where the supplier sells tangible personal property and exports them from Canada, or where the non-resident recipient exports them directly from Canada after purchase. The BC LP must not know or be indifferent that the goods will be diverted for Canadian consumption; delivery to a foreign destination must be substantiated. Services, if any, are zero-rated only where supplied to a non-resident and not performed in Canada. For BC PST, no PST applies when goods are shipped outside British Columbia for delivery outside the province, provided the sale completes in export and is appropriately documented.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (Export Reporting System reference or approved self-classified export document, where filing thresholds apply) identifying the goods, destination, value, and HS classification (likely under HS 95.04/95.06 for games/gaming equipment)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill and commercial invoice with packing list showing physical export movement from Canada to the non-resident purchaser

Inward Remittance Certificate / bank or payment-rail settlement report (Stripe/Kickstarter/PayPal payout statement, wire confirmation, or FX inward remittance) proving gross export consideration was received in the seller's account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is accepted only if documentary evidence is retained and traceable to the specific export sale. If CRA or BC's tax auditor cannot link the invoice to actual export and FX receipt, the sale is recharacterized as a taxable domestic supply; GST (5%) and BC PST (7%) are clawed back with statutory interest. False or grossly negligent statements attract a civil penalty of 25% of the understated net tax (minimum C$100) under s. 285.1 ETA, while deliberate schemes may be prosecuted under s. 327 ETA; refunds claimed on fraudulent export documentation are denied and can be recaptured within four years, or without time limit for misrepresentation or fraud. For BC PST, the provincial uncollected-tax liability is reassessed and penalties/interest apply from the original due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted capital and current account convertibility. Profit remittances to non-resident limited partners are permitted without prior approval or capital controls, subject solely to standard beneficial ownership verification, tax reporting obligations under the Income Tax Act, and FINTRAC compliance. No exchange controls apply to routine corporate treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion requirements exist for export receipts. Canadian exporters retain full discretion to utilize foreign currency proceeds. No statutory timelines, conversion ratios, or surrender mandates apply; voluntary surrender to authorized dealers is available but optional.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible via regulated digital platforms such as Wise Business or Revolut Business for cross-border EMIs, subject to FINTRAC registration, full AML/KYC obligations, and compliance with the Common Reporting Standard. Offshore digital EMIs require structuring to prevent triggering foreign asset reporting or sanctions screening; direct bank-issued crypto or high-risk fintech corridors remain restricted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video KYC and electronic signing are permitted for eligible limited partnerships under updated FINTRAC and OSFI guidelines. Directors and authorized signers must complete video interviews or in-person verification for transactions exceeding standard thresholds; physical presence is not mandated for routine onboarding but may be required for complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds originating from gaming accessories sales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, Kickstarter and PayPal transaction histories, revenue forecasts, director affidavits, and contracts demonstrating legitimate tabletop gaming operations
Foreign ownership declaration, passport and proof-of-address copies, beneficial ownership register, and partnership agreement excerpts

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections utilize SWIFT wire transfers with purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification requires supporting documentation including the limited partnership agreement, investor subscription agreements, and CRA-compliant tax forms. All transfers must comply with FINTRAC registration thresholds and beneficial ownership disclosure requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements route through SWIFT MT103 messages referencing specific invoices. Commercial Letters of Credit may be arranged via correspondent banks for larger exposures. Purpose codes include 'Trade Payment' or invoice-specific references. All disbursements require proper invoicing, export documentation where applicable, and full AML/KYC compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for speculative or hedging purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Service BC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50; continued default for 2 consecutive years exposes the limited partnership to administrative strike-off, loss of authority to carry on business, and loss of limited liability protection for limited partners.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit requirement for British Columbia limited partnerships; an audit is mandatory only if the partnership agreement so provides, or if a court or the Registrar so directs on application by a limited partner; no revenue-based audit threshold applies under the Limited Partnership Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for a non-publicly accountable limited partnership; IFRS is required only if the limited partnership is publicly accountable or specifically elects IFRS in the partnership agreement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual report must confirm the current general partner and list the limited partners, their contribution amounts, and any changes during the preceding year; transfers of limited partnership interests must also be evidenced by an amending declaration filed with BC Registries, making the annual report the equivalent of the annual UBO confirmatory filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300–$750 for registered address and regulatory agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $5,000–$12,000 for a private limited partnership with annual revenue below USD 5 million

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined for ordinary corporations (15% federal + 12% British Columbia); the Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent, so income is taxed at the partner level at applicable personal or corporate marginal rates
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC small business deduction (9% federal + 2% BC = 11% combined) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (35% for CCPCs); BC Training Tax Credit (10% refundable for qualifying small-business training expenditures)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return; filed via CRA EFILE/EIAP certified software or by mail to the CRA Surrey Tax Centre; partner slips (T5013 SUMMARY and individual partner schedules) issued to every partner
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (s. 229 ITA); a December 31 fiscal year-end therefore requires filing by May 31 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (loss) from the casting and sale of tabletop polyhedral dice, including pre-sale crowdfunding receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership's Canadian-source business income allocated to non-resident partners is reported here and in the partner allocation boxes; non-resident partners must file a Canadian income return to claim treaty relief

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal, wholesale, and retail sales of dice and gaming accessories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross revenue; export sales sourced under s. 3(e) allocation rules and any cross-border e-commerce supplies must be separately tracked for GST and income tax purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible business expenses: epoxy resin, silicone molds, pigment, packaging, shipping, platform commissions, payment-processing fees, and marketing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be arm's-length, reasonable, and supported by invoices; allocations to non-resident partners must follow the Limited Partnership agreement and s. 96 ITA

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance (CCA) on moulds, 3D printers, casting equipment, and computer hardware (CCA classes 8, 43, and 53)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CCA computed under s. 1100 of the Income Tax Regulations; accelerated investment incentive (AII) half-year rules apply; each partner's share of CCA is reported on the partner's T5013 schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner identification, percentages of allocation, and each partner's share of net income or loss as set out in the LP agreement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every non-resident partner, country of tax residence, and share percentage; this supports Part XIII characterization and establishes eligibility for treaty-reduced rates

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: $25 per day late-filing penalty on the T5013 (minimum $100, maximum $2,500); $25 per day per missing or incorrect partner schedule (minimum $100, up to $2,500); gross negligence penalty under s. 163(2) equal to 50% of understated tax; willful evasion under s. 239 carries fines of 50% to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: GST34 GST/HST Return; filed via CRA GST/HST NETFILE or the My Business Account portal; BC PST is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, quarterly, or monthly depending on taxable revenue thresholds
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filers must file within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (s. 228(3) ETA); instalments are required once annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,500,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales and other revenue; 5% federal GST applies in British Columbia, with 7% PST collected separately
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: GST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable sales exceed CAD 30,000 in any calendar quarter or four consecutive quarters; qualifying export sales of dice are zero-rated

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST/HST collected or collectible on Canadian taxable supplies of dice and gaming accessories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: GST must be remitted on all Canadian supplies regardless of the payment platform used (Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal); platform platform fees do not reduce the GST collectible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input tax credits (ITCs) claimed on business purchases such as epoxy resin, molds, equipment, shipping, and third-party manufacturing services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership claims ITCs on behalf of the whole venture; a non-resident partner cannot claim a share of ITCs on a separate return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty from 1% to 6% of net tax based on the overdue period, plus daily compound interest; failure to register carries a penalty of 5% of net tax plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months); general partner and director liability applies under s. 323 ETA

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding rate (s. 212(2) ITA) applies to dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents; for a Limited Partnership, profit distributions are not dividends — non-resident partners are taxed on their allocated share of Canadian-source business income under Part I, and actual cash distributions representing previously taxed income or return of capital are generally not subject to further withholding
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty reduction, the non-resident partner must obtain a current Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction and submit it together with the applicable CRA form (NR301, NR302, NR303, or Form RC471) to the partnership or directly to the CRA; the CRA reviews the claim, applies the reduced rate at source, or processes a refund in the non-resident partner's Canadian return; the TRC must cover each calendar year in which relief is claimed and must be retained in the partnership's books for audit purposes
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 25% on both interest and royalties (Part XIII, s. 212(1) ITA). Under the Canada–US Treaty, interest is exempt (Article XI) and royalties are limited to 10% (Article XII); most modern Canadian treaties provide 0–15% royalty rates and 0% interest rates. The partnership must withhold at source on all cross-border interest and royalty payments made by the partnership business to non-residents, regardless of treaty eligibility, unless a waiver has been granted

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 — aggregate fair-market value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with any single non-resident in a taxation year triggers mandatory Form T106 filing and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (s. 247(4)); Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue above CAD 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245 ITA) disallows tax benefits from transactions lacking genuine economic substance where the main purpose is tax avoidance; the Supreme Court of Canada's Copthorne test requires a real economic result. Under s. 65 of the BC Partnership Act, a limited partner who takes part in the control or management of the partnership loses limited liability and is treated as a general partner, so the LP's actual commercial activity must align with the filed partnership agreement and tax filings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Kickstarter, Stripe, or PayPal sales revenue, fabricating epoxy resin or mold expenses, or concealing the identity of non-resident partners in the T5013
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s. 239 ITA: fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years; civil reassessment with arrears interest under s. 161 and a 50% gross-negligence penalty under s. 163(2)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners are jointly and severally liable for the partnership's tax debts; directors of a corporate general partner are personally liable under s. 227.1 for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST; the CRA may seek civil travel bans, bank account freezes, and enforcement against personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated non-filing of the T5013 or GST/HST returns, or collecting GST on dice sales and failing to remit it to the CRA
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: T5013 late filing: $25 per day up to $2,500; GST/HST late filing: 1% to 6% of net tax plus daily interest; prosecution under s. 238 ITA carries fines from $1,000 to $25,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 ITA and s. 323 ETA for unremitted amounts; the CRA can issue requirement payments to Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal and seize the partnership's bank accounts

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dice to a related offshore distributor below arm's-length market price, or paying inflated royalties to a related foreign IP-holding entity without contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s. 247(3) ITA re-determination of the arm's-length price; 10% penalty on the net transfer-pricing adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000) for failure to provide documentation; unresolved double taxation subject only to Mutual Agreement Procedure relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the mispricing may be personally assessed where gross negligence is established; personal assets of directors of the corporate general partner may be pursued in civil collections

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a BC Limited Partnership with no real commercial operations, using opaque ownership to launder crowdfunding or PayPal proceeds, or a limited partner exercising management control over the dice-casting business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA administrative monetary penalty up to CAD 2,000,000 for FINTRAC non-compliance; Criminal Code s. 462.31 money-laundering offence with imprisonment up to 10 years; GAAR under s. 245 cancels tax benefits; the BC Registrar may strike the LP from the registry
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A limited partner who participates in control becomes personally liable for all partnership debts under s. 65 of the BC Partnership Act; directors of the corporate general partner face unlimited liability, asset seizure, and deregistration consequences
